name: CVB / Marketing Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / CVB/Marketing Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, October 15, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  October 15, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells, Deputy City Manager
  Keith Sterling, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis, Beverly
  Hills Conference and Visitors Bureau CEO Julie Wagner

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Review of Beverly Hills Tourism Economic & Fiscal Impacts, and Visitor Profile
  Study for Calendar Year 2023:
  a. Presentation by Julie Wagner:
  i. 2.3 million less people visited the City in 2023 than in 2018, Mostly due to
  a lack of international travelers.
  ii. LA Tourism does not anticipate international tourism to recover to 2019
  levels until 2025 due to several things, particularly Visa wait times and a
  strong dollar.
  iii. This has resulted in depressed sales tax revenue, as international tourists
  tend to stay longer and spend more in the City.
  b. The City’s federal lobbyist is lobbying for measures to decrease Visa waiting times.

  3) Beverly Hills Conference and Visitors Bureau (CVB) Updates on Fiscal Year 2024-
  25 Programs and Initiatives:
  a. Presentation by Julie Wagner:
  i. The CVB is unable to present the Q4 Visa credit card information as it is
  not available yet.
  ii. July had strong occupancy and RevPAR numbers; however our
  competitors have 15%-20% higher occupancy rates.
  iii. August was slightly worse than last year, but that is mostly due to Taylor
  Swift causing a bump in 2023 numbers.
  iv. The FY 23/24 initiative with Brand USA Canada Co-op had a $60,900
  investment for a return of $175,730.
 Highlights for October 15, 2024
CVB/Marketing Committee

  v. The /Imagine Beverly Hills AI Campaign is planned to launch in January
  2025.
  vi. The June 2024 Middle East Sales Mission saw approximately $200,000 in
  hotel bookings for Hotels in the City, and business from the region is up
  YOY.
  vii. Q4 23-24 Destination Group Sales activity generated 35 leads and
  $4.655,250 in lead revenue. However booked revenue was $2.1 million
  viii. Press Highlights from last fiscal year include Luxury Women Leaders to
  Watch in 2025, Thrillist, ARRIVED Magazine, Visit CA, tea influencer
  collaborations, and PR Newsletter distributions. These stories were worth
  $8 million in ad value in Q4 alone.
  ix. The Fall Summer Extended campaign ran from August 19 – October 13.
  x. The CVB contributed $40,000 to the Visit California Fall campaign, the
  results of which are expected in February.
  xi. The holiday 2024 campaign will run from November 11 through December
  31. This will include a 6-week TV schedule with a budget of $75,000
  xii. The theme for the Spring 2025 campaign will be A World Away from
  Greater LA.
  xiii. The CVB is looking at having a Spa Week promotion in January 2025,
  which would be a partnership between the CVB and Hotels.
  xiv. CVB Travel Trade activities for Q1 and Q2 of FY 24-25 included ILTM
  Singapore, Visit California Luxury Forum, ILTM Europe, Maritz Activate,
  Northstar, and IMEX.
  xv. The New York Sales Mission will be on October 23.
  xvi. The CVB originally expected to have a carryover of $250,000 from FY 23-
  24, their actual carryover was $331,484 and would like to use the funds to
  add a group sales position. The current group sales position is a salaried
  employee who is currently overloaded.
  xvii. The CVB is currently focused on domestic group Sales, but they are doing
  one overseas initiative with LA tourism.
  xviii. The CVB is adding an AI Chatbot to its website as well as additional back-
  end improvements.
  xix. The CVB is also preparing a Centennial for Route 66 for FY 2025-26.
  xx. Both Liaisons are in support of the revised carryover budget.

  4) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: October 15, 2024 / 4:20 PM
